title: First time showing this off. Gutter Scrap, build a mech out of trash.
author: Mekkablood
selftext:
This was made in Opus 5.5, no other external programs other than three.js. Feel free to ask anything about the development. Will be back to answer them later tonight.

Just some colored pencils, mechs, drones, and trash. It's a linear game that takes place in a chaotic city where law enforcement has abandoned.

Through the anarchy a general has taken control and taken out your scrap yard. Time to take it back. [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5541720/Gutter\_Scrap/?beta=0](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5541720/Gutter_Scrap/?beta=0)

comments.author: Fishy53
comments.body: How have you been building your animations and rigging? I've been making a modular mech game for a few weeks now and getting good models and the rigging have been a pain in me arse!

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body:
The best way I have found is to use Opus 5.5 on max. Have it build the model and not use a separate program, and then bitch at it till it gets the animation right(same thing with the initial model design). Opus can do damn near anything you just have to be really specific about what you don't like.

It's a slow expensive process though for sure.

replies.author: Fishy53
replies.body: Well it's good to know theres light at the end of the tunnel then. How much of your usage does it take to make a model?

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: For a single model? Not much at all, but adds up when it's 20+.

comments.author: lawlshawk
comments.body:
Cool to see another three.js game headed to Steam. What are you wrapping it in for the desktop build... Electron, Tauri, something else?  
  
We went with Tauri and it's been basically painless so far, small builds since it uses the system webview instead of bundling a browser. The catch is that webview is different per OS (WebView2 on Windows, WebKit on mac/Linux), so test Windows early if that's not your main machine.

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: I think Electron, it's whatever Opus uses when you ask it for a Steam build.
